summary: The most important signals this week come from fusion and from tokenisation infrastructure. On the fusion side, Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) formally set its fusion power-demonstration subsidies: Starlight Engine (19 November) is to receive up to 23.3 billion yen, and Helical Fusion (18 November) up to about 19.2 billion yen (about $126 million). France released a 2026–2035 national fusion strategy on 16 November, and the ITER Council on 18–19 November confirmed that 6 of 9 vacuum-vessel sector modules are in place. On the quantum-energy side, the first quantum magnetic-sensing cable-inspection device developed by State Grid Zhejiang Electric Power Research Institute was used on 20 November for the first time to inspect a 25.7 km low-frequency submarine cable, taking about one day; the US Department of Energy issued a request for information on 17 November on cryogenic and "quantum–HPC integration" testbeds (closing 17 December). On the RWA side, the Monetary Authority of Singapore announced on 19 November that it had natively issued S$100 million of tokenised MAS bills settled in wholesale central-bank digital currency, and released the Guardian tokenised-collateral framework; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority deepened Ensemble cooperation with Swift on 16 November on cross-border tokenised deposits; and Germany's DZ BANK on 17 November settled NRW.BANK ethereum-tokenised securities in central-bank money via the ECB's Pontes. No verified large new energy-asset RWA issuance was found this week.
trends: Public fusion funding is arriving faster: METI this week set subsidies of up to 23.3 billion yen and about 19.2 billion yen for two private companies; France's ten-year strategy aims to double the number of master's students and raise doctoral theses by 50%; ITER has completed 212 first-level milestones (target 202). The about $4.5 billion of annual private fusion financing cited in last week's IAEA report is now pairing with government money in a "public–private dual track".

Quantum energy is diverging: quantum sensing has entered actual grid operations (the Zhejiang submarine-cable inspection was completed in about one day, 3–4 days shorter than conventional methods), while the quantum-computing side is still building infrastructure (a US DOE quantum–HPC testbed RFI, closing 17 December). No new empirical evidence that quantum computing outperforms classical methods on the grid was found this week.

Tokenisation has entered a "settlement in central-bank money" stage: Singapore (S$100 million of tokenised MAS bills, wholesale CBDC settlement), the euro area (DZ BANK settling eWpG securities via Pontes) and Hong Kong (Ensemble × Swift cross-border tokenised deposits) all advanced in the same week. Settlement infrastructure is becoming a core point of competition for RWAs.

Energy RWAs are still mostly small-scale or promotional: this week's search found no verified large new tokenisation of energy assets. A promotional piece appeared in the same period for a carbon-credit token (for example a 17 November Way.CZ "WCZ CCQ" token) that did not disclose an audit of underlying assets or regulatory information, and should be strictly distinguished from licensed projects.

To watch next week: according to The Block (11 November), the US OKXICE tokenised-securities venue plans to go live on 23 November under an SEC "innovation exemption"; the EU ETSG membership call and the bid opening for China Southern Power Grid's quantum-clearing project both fall on 27 November.
footer: All facts and figures in this brief are taken from the public sources listed. The METI amounts are maximum subsidy figures; France's strategy has not yet announced additional budget; the US DOE document is a request for information and is not a funding commitment; the OKXICE launch date is a planned date reported by the media. Institutions mentioned are an observation list only and do not constitute any investment or partnership recommendation. Time window: 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-20 (Zurich time).

items.title: Japan's METI formally sets fusion power-demonstration subsidies: up to 23.3 billion yen for Starlight Engine and up to about 19.2 billion yen for Helical Fusion
items.what: On 19 November, Starlight Engine (SLE) announced that, after a conditional selection, it had been formally selected for a Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry subsidy under the fiscal 2025 supplementary budget for a "fusion power generation demonstration project". Together with group company Kyoto Fusioneering, it will carry out a "high-temperature superconducting tokamak power-generation demonstration project", with a maximum subsidy of 23.3 billion yen for fiscal years 2026–2028, covering 10 areas including plant integration, HTS coils, the divertor, heating, tritium fuel, blanket and power-generation systems, remote maintenance, materials, handling of activated materials, and diagnostics and control, with the aim of a fusion power demonstration on the FAST device in the 2030s. The day before (18 November), Helical Fusion announced formal selection under the same METI subsidy programme, with a maximum of about 19.2 billion yen (about $126 million) through February 2029, for manufacturing and assembly of the integrated demonstration device Helix HARUKA, basic design of the first plant Helix KANATA, and key components. Including this subsidy, its cumulative financing and commitments are about 33.2 billion yen (about $218 million); stage one of HARUKA is planned to include an HTS-coil energisation test in 2027.
items.why: This is the first time the Japanese government has awarded large, multi-year subsidies to private fusion companies with power demonstration as the goal. The two awards together have a maximum of more than 42 billion yen, with funds directed explicitly to engineering steps such as blankets, the fuel cycle, maintenance and materials. Together with last week's UK STEP procurement, this shows that major countries are moving from research grants toward engineering and supply-chain build-out.
items.src: Starlight Engine press release / Helical Fusion (Business Wire)

items.title: France releases a 2026–2035 national fusion strategy, aiming at a European-scale demonstration reactor; the ITER Council confirms that 6 of 9 vacuum-vessel modules are in place
items.what: According to The Duck Curve, citing ITER, France's minister for higher education, research and space, Philippe Baptiste, released a 2026–2035 national fusion strategy on 16 November at CEA's WEST tokamak: magnetic confinement as the main line, inertial confinement (the Laser Mégajoule facility) as a complement; 2026–2030 to consolidate research and infrastructure, strengthen talent and lock in follow-on funding; 2031–2035 to prepare the design of a demonstration reactor in a European framework and start construction, possibly at Cadarache. French fusion programmes currently amount to about €70 million a year and about 400 full-time equivalents (excluding an ITER contribution of about €150 million a year); the strategy's goals include doubling the number of master's students and raising doctoral theses by 50%. On 18–19 November, the 39th ITER Council meeting announced that 6 of 9 vacuum-vessel sector modules had been installed in the tokamak pit, with the seventh expected this month; 212 first-level milestones have been completed (target 202), and the first gyrotron pulses have succeeded, with long-pulse operation beginning.
items.why: France has written fusion into a ten-year national strategy and set explicit talent-expansion targets, while ITER construction is ahead of the 2024 baseline. European fusion is forming a three-layer pattern of national strategy, international big science and private companies. The first phase of the strategy still includes "locking in funding", however, and no additional budget figure has been given.
items.src: The Duck Curve (citing ITER) / ITER Organization

items.title: State Grid Zhejiang Electric Power Research Institute's first quantum magnetic-sensing cable-inspection device is used for the first time on a low-frequency submarine cable: 25.7 km completed in about one day
items.what: According to a CCTV News client report (reprinted by China News Service) on 20 November, State Grid Zhejiang Electric Power Research Institute, after two years of lead development, used the country's first quantum magnetic-sensing cable-inspection device that day for the first smart inspection of China's first 35 kV low-frequency submarine cable, commissioned in 2022, connecting Dachen Island in Taizhou with Jinqing Town in Luqiao, about 25.7 km in length. The device can be carried on a drone, on the "Guojiao-1" unmanned boat with a draught of only 0.5 metres, and on a robot dog, collecting magnetic-field data from air, water and land. Technicians said positioning accuracy can reach metre level and detection depth can cover water a hundred metres deep; the whole cable can be inspected in about one day, 3 to 4 days shorter than conventional methods.
items.why: Unlike "quantum computing to optimise the grid", which is still at the benchmark stage, quantum sensing has entered actual work in grid operations, with a quantifiable efficiency measure (inspection time falling from about 4–5 days to about 1 day). This is currently the quantum-energy direction closest to commercial value.
items.src: CCTV News client / China News Service

items.title: The US Department of Energy seeks comments on national testbeds for cryogenic technology and "quantum–HPC integration", closing on 17 December
items.what: According to The Quantum Insider on 17 November, the Advanced Scientific Computing Research (ASCR) programme in the US Department of Energy's Office of Science issued a request for information (RFI) seeking industry and research comments on two related testbeds: a cryogenic-technology testbed, and a testbed integrating quantum computers with classical high-performance computing systems, covering quantum computing, quantum sensing, cryogenic electronics and the integration of quantum processors with conventional computing. The request asks for technical needs, scalable infrastructure design, estimated costs and models of cooperation; replies close on 17 December. This is a request for information, not a tender, and is not a commitment to fund or to hold a competition.
items.why: The Department of Energy is planning "quantum + supercomputing" as shared national infrastructure, consistent with last week's German QUANDA work connecting a trapped-ion machine to HPC and TU Delft's linking of DelftBlue and Quantum Inspire. The bottleneck in quantum-energy applications is shifting from algorithms toward hardware–software integration and shared platforms.

items.title: The Monetary Authority of Singapore natively issues S$100 million of tokenised MAS bills settled in wholesale CBDC, and releases the Guardian tokenised-collateral framework
items.what: On 19 November the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) announced that on 6 November it had natively issued S$100 million of 4-week tokenised MAS bills on the Singapore dollar test network it operates, settled in wholesale central-bank digital currency, with five primary dealers taking part: DBS, HSBC Singapore, OCBC, Standard Chartered Singapore and UOB. The network will be renamed SG Digital Ledger and positioned as operational infrastructure. The same day, MAS and industry released the Guardian Tokenised Collateral Framework, covering operational requirements across the collateral life cycle, including eligibility, custody, valuation, return and enforcement. In a keynote at Singapore FinTech Festival, MAS Managing Director Chia Der Jiun said the scale of tokenised financial assets is still small relative to traditional markets, and that scale-up needs commercially attractive use cases, trusted digital money and interoperable settlement infrastructure, and announced that the GL1 organisation had been established in Singapore.
items.why: This is a live case of native issuance plus settlement in central-bank money at the central-bank level, and it standardises legal and operational requirements for tokenised collateral. If energy and green-asset tokenisation is to enter institutional markets, it will ultimately need to meet the same collateral and settlement standards.

items.title: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority deepens cooperation with Swift: exploring interoperability between the Ensemble settlement layer and the Swift ledger, using multi-currency tokenised deposits for cross-border payments
items.what: On 16 November the Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced deeper cooperation with Swift, together with Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered Hong Kong and HSBC, to explore interoperability between the Swift ledger and the Ensemble project's settlement layer, and to develop a cross-border payment mechanism using multi-currency tokenised deposits. The two sides have studied interoperability of central-bank digital currency systems in the Ensemble sandbox since 2023. HKMA Deputy Chief Executive Howard Lee said Ensemble TX had entered a new stage of advancing the tokenisation ecosystem, and that cooperation with Swift further extends Ensemble's connections with international financial institutions.
items.why: Hong Kong tokenisation is extending from local 24/7 settlement in central-bank money (last month's Ensemble TX) to cross-border interoperability. For cross-border energy and green-asset transactions, whether the settlement leg can be completed across borders on tokenised deposits is a precondition for RWAs to reach scale.

items.title: DZ BANK settles NRW.BANK ethereum-tokenised securities in central-bank money via the ECB's Pontes
items.what: On 17 November, DZ BANK announced that it had invested in tokenised securities issued by NRW.BANK on Ethereum under Germany's Electronic Securities Act (eWpG), with payment made directly in central-bank money through the Pontes bridge introduced by the ECB at the end of September, achieving delivery versus payment (DvP): the tokenised securities are locked on-chain and transfer automatically once payment in central-bank money is confirmed, with no intermediary. The transaction uses the Smart Bond Contract (SBC) mechanism developed by DZ BANK and first piloted in March, mapping the full life cycle of issuance, interest and redemption on-chain; the March pilot had used the Deutsche Bundesbank's Trigger solution as an interim step.
items.why: The euro area now has a usable channel for "public-chain tokenised securities + settlement in central-bank money". Combined with last week's ETSG standards call, EU tokenisation is moving from pilots toward infrastructure. Future tokenised issues of European green bonds or energy project bonds may be able to use this path directly.
